Thanks, Marissa — appreciate the summary and the doc. A few clarifying questions from our side after reviewing briefly:

1) Controller/Processor: Confirming Acme Health will be the Controller and Redwood will be a Processor for request/response handling and any derived artifacts. We expect that to be explicit in the DPA.

2) Embeddings / Model Outputs: Are embeddings considered customer data under the DPA footprint? Specifically: if we send PII in prompts and request embeddings, will Redwood store those embeddings by default?

3) Logs & Retention: Our security team prefers 30-day max retention for request/response logs and telemetry; is that the default or can we shorten it? We also want the ability to disable storage for sensitive endpoints.

4) Subprocessors: Please provide the current list of subprocessors and confirm the notice window before adding new ones. We typically ask for 30 days notice.

5) Breach Notice: We expect initial notification within 72 hours of discovery with an update cadence thereafter. Is that feasible?

6) Deletion on Termination: We need confirmation that customer data will be purged within a specified window after contract termination unless otherwise scoped.

If you can get Vivek and Neha to weigh in on the technical/legal items that would be great — happy to hop on another short call if needed.

—Samir
Senior InfoSec Program Manager | Acme Health

Hi Samir / Olivia — following up with technical clarifications (short version):

- Embeddings/model outputs: By default, Redwood treats request inputs, generated outputs, and derived artifacts (including embeddings) as customer data. For hosted mode, short-term KV cache and request logs are retained to support inference performance and troubleshooting.

- Retention options: Default request/response and telemetry retention is 30 days for hosted accounts. We can shorten retention (down to 0 days for request bodies) for specific routes or customers via config, or eliminate storage entirely by using Redwood Dedicated/Private (customer-managed deployment).

- Logs: We separate (1) access logs (IP, timestamps) retained per infra policy; (2) request/response logs (prompt + model output) kept under customer retention settings; (3) aggregated telemetry (no PII) used for platform health.

- Data residency: For strict residency needs we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private. For hosted accounts, we can pin processing to a region (e.g., us-east-1) and provide contractual residency commitments in the DPA/contract where feasible.

- Encryption: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). Keys are managed by Redwood; customer-managed KMS is available for Private deployments.

I'm attaching our security questionnaire response for your review (security_questionnaire_responses.xlsx). Happy to provide a short runbook showing how to configure zero-retention for sensitive routes.

—Neha Kapoor
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: security_questionnaire_responses.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Post-call — DPA clarifications & next steps

Hi Samir / Olivia — thanks for the questions. A few legal clarifications and proposed DPA language to address your bullets: 

- Controller/Processor: Redwood will accept Processor role for the processing activities described in the DPA; Acme Health remains Controller. We will add an explicit clause to that effect in the DPA preamble.

- Subprocessors: We maintain a current list at https://redwoodinference.com/subprocessors and will provide a copy with the DPA. Redwood will notify customers at least 30 days prior to engaging a new subprocessor; in urgent cases (e.g., security patching), we will provide notice "as soon as reasonably practicable" and allow for termination rights where required.

- Breach notification: Redwood will notify Acme Health of confirmed breaches impacting Acme data without undue delay and will provide initial information within 72 hours of becoming aware where practicable. We'll include an obligation to provide ongoing updates and remediation support.

- Retention & Deletion: Proposed: Redwood to purge customer-identifiable request/response data within 60 days of contract termination, unless the parties agree otherwise. For retention shorter than the hosted default, we will add language permitting configuration or a service-level commitment for Dedicated/Private customers.

- Subprocessor liability / audit: We can commit to use of contractual flow-downs to subprocessors and provide SOC 2 reports under NDA; for on-site audits, we can discuss scope for Dedicated/Private customers.

If the above aligns, I will incorporate these bullets as redlines into the attached DPA and share a DocuSign link for signature. Otherwise please flag any specific language you'd like adjusted.

Thanks — Vivek
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
